title: Machine learning brain age is higher in amnestic mild cognitive impairment
summary: A machine learning brain age model trained on T1 MRI of 974 healthy controls was tested on held-out controls and patients with amnestic mild cognitive impairment from two cohorts (BABRI, ADNI). Patients had higher predicted age difference than controls, associated with cognition, APOE e4 carriers and amyloid-positive status, and combined with other Alzheimer markers gave an AUC of 0.87 for progression. Retrospective and associational.
ai_technology: Machine learning brain age prediction model on T1-weighted MRI
organization: Beijing Normal University (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Neuroscience and Learning; Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative Centre)

evidence.tested: Held-out controls and patients from two independent cohorts (BABRI and ADNI).
evidence.unknown: Causal interpretation and clinical use of predicted age difference are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A machine learning model estimated brain age from MRI to quantify deviation from healthy aging.
